title: ADHD Time: Why It's Always Now or Never #Shorts
description: If you have ADHD, time doesn't feel like a timeline — it feels like two states: NOW and NOT NOW. That's why deadlines three weeks away feel invisible, and deadlines tomorrow feel like emergencies. This is a real neurological difference in how the ADHD brain processes future time, not laziness or poor planning. Follow for daily ADHD content.

voiceover: You have one appointment at 3pm and your entire day is gone. That is Waiting Mode. When one fixed event sits on your calendar, your brain treats everything before it as unscheduled limbo. Here is what it looks like: You cancel a morning workout because the appointment is 'coming up.' You sit at your desk for two hours but open nothing. You refresh your phone seventeen times and call it waiting. Your brain can not start a new thing when it knows an interruption is coming. Follow for daily ADHD content.

title: Waiting Mode: Why One Task Freezes Your Whole Day #Shorts
description:
Waiting Mode is a common ADHD pattern where one fixed event on your calendar puts your entire brain into a holding state — making it nearly impossible to start anything else before it. If you have ever lost a whole morning to a single afternoon appointment, this is why. Understanding the real mechanism behind Waiting Mode is the first step to working with your brain instead of against it.
